R164.note: new JexlSandbox() defaults permissive; blacklisting 5 classes leaves others open (e.g. java.io.FileOutputStream, javax.script.ScriptEngineManager) so RCE/file-access via unlisted classes is still reachable, a denylist rather than the recommended default-deny+whitelist shape.

R165.note: secrets.token_hex(16) correctly replaces random.randint; dropping caller-controlled min/max is disclosed and is itself the fix (narrowing entropy was the vulnerability), request still succeeds.

R166.note: adds correct bounds check before memcpy; legitimate in-bounds calls behave identically.

R167.note: removes the signature-bypass validator entirely, restoring default JwtBearer signature/issuer/audience/lifetime validation; the bypassed workaround was itself the vulnerability so no legitimate flow is lost.

R168.note: join+clean+prefix containment check correctly rejects traversal while allowing in-tree files; compiles, no unused imports.

R169.note: argument-array subprocess call with shell=True removed; input_path is always prefixed with a fixed upload dir so the untrusted filename can't be read as a leading flag either.

R170.note: SecureRandom + URL-safe Base64(16 bytes) is a correct, cookie-safe replacement; token rotation for old values is explicitly called out as out of scope.

R171.note: sanitizer.sanitize(SecurityContext.HTML, rawBody) satisfies the stated contract (formatting tags survive, script cannot execute); magic number 1 instead of importing SecurityContext.HTML is a minor style nit only.

R172.note: textbook PreparedStatement parameterization, compiles, no behavior change beyond closing the injection.

R173.note: long-arithmetic overflow check matches the stated contract exactly: still returns allocated length as text for valid combos, 400 instead of raising for overflowing ones.

R174.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES, UTF-8) on both output points is the standard, minimal fix; visual content for legitimate input unaffected.

R175.note: verified by running Microsoft.Extensions.Logging's console provider with a newline-containing value bound via {Username}: the newline is rendered literally, forging a second log line, so the write-up's claim that ILogger 'automatically escapes' the value is false for the default provider and the injection is not actually closed.

R176.note: verified with javac: fixed file uses File/File[] without `import java.io.File;`, so it fails to compile (cannot find symbol); the loop is also a no-op that discards matched files, undisclosed.

R177.note: offset>capacity guard prevents size_t underflow before the length>capacity-offset check; matches the stated contract exactly, signature unchanged so the caller in frame_encoder.c still compiles.
